newsitem.title: USA: Cold, wet weather delays Iowa fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: Cold, wet weather delays Iowa fieldwork.

text.p: Cold and snow kept Iowa farmers out of the fields for most of the week ended Sunday, Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop report.
"Frozen ground in many areas stopped field work and many farmers are now worried about getting a late start on row-crop plantings," the weekly report said.
Statewide, 1.3 days were rated suitable for fieldwork.
As of Sunday, 45 percent of the primary seedbed preparations, including work done last fall, were complete, behind the five-year average of 49 percent
Oat plantings were 38 percent complete, about four days behind the five-year average of 45 percent.

Winter wheat was rated one percent very poor, three percent poor, 36 percent fair, 52 percent good and eight percent excellent. Crop reporters expected about three percent of the winter wheat would be lost due to winterkill.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, two percent short, 73 percent adequate and 25 percent surplus.
